newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares shuffle higher but market reluctant.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares shuffle higher but market reluctant.

text.p: Oslo shares tip-toed slightly higher on Wednesday as sharply firmer Norwegian bonds and large gains in industrial giant Norsk Hydro helped to drag the reluctant market higher, dealers said.

The lack of an interest rate move by the U.S. Federal Reserve failed to inspire a response and investor cautiousness was likely to remain until after the presentation of Norway's national budget on October 4, they said.
Oslo's Total share index edged up 0.1 percent to close around mid range at 841.31 points. Turnover was a moderate 676 million crowns.
High oil prices and a slight improvement in aluminium helped reverse recent losses on Norsk Hydro, which advanced six crowns in a late spurt to 310 crowns.
But the steam ran out of this week's rally by shipbuilder, engineering and construction group Kvaerner, which retreated six crowns in the A stock to 248 crowns.
Dealers said the Central Bank's quarterly inflation report met market expectations and concerns over future rises in consumer prices due to wage growth remained high.
But all eyes would be on the government's 1997 budget proposal, they said.
